translations.t0000: Favre built scratch-01 and scratch-02, is aware of their missing audit integration, and managed the migration including INFRA-2291 — he possessed the most complete technical knowledge of the entire relevant infrastructure.
translations.t0001: Favre had been working in breach of contract for a startup in Winterthur since June (approx. CHF 400/week). This open disciplinary risk could be interpreted as a motive for additional income. Card transactions show multiple purchases in Winterthur.
translations.t0002: The publication on Confluence was a good-faith documentation act that Favre volunteered during the interview and immediately regretted. Iris Ammann confirmed that documenting it was correct — only the permission level was wrong. As a result, the knowledge became accessible to 8 additional accounts, which widens the pool of potential perpetrators but does not directly incriminate Favre.
translations.t0003: Favre explicitly acknowledges the mistake and describes good-faith intent.
translations.t0004: Iris Ammann confirms: documenting was correct, only the permission level was the problem.
translations.t0005: The investigator notes that Favre volunteered both incriminating points without being prompted.
translations.t0006: Favre delayed remediation of the overly broad dr-export-ro scope for months despite repeated reminders from Iris Ammann; the ticket remained open until after the exfiltration.
translations.t0007: Technical knowledge of scratch and the infrastructure is not exclusive to the perpetrator in this case: the Confluence page, the public ticket INFRA-2291, and approximately 40 people were aware of the logging window. Furthermore, Favre was physically in Val Müstair throughout the entire time of the offence, as evidenced by multiple independent sources (his own Slack messages from Val Müstair during the offence window, Lukas Hofer's statement about the 4-hour video call on Saturday, automatic out-of-office reply active from Thursday 18:05).
translations.t0008: On Thursday afternoon, Favre publicly announces his absence in Val Müstair — before the start of the offence period.
translations.t0009: Automatic out-of-office reply active from Thursday 18:05 documents a planned and announced absence.
translations.t0010: Favre writes at 13:11 local time on Saturday from Val Müstair and explicitly states that he has no car and is dependent on the PostBus.
translations.t0011: Lukas Hofer independently confirms Favre's presence in Val Müstair and the video call on Saturday.
translations.t0012: Lukas Hofer publicly thanks Favre in the incident channel on Saturday at 17:48, which confirms the video call.
translations.t0013: Favre immediately disputes the scratch-02 anomaly ticket by citing his location.
translations.t0014: Forensics cannot establish the identity of the perpetrator — neither Favre nor anyone else. The absence of operator identification is not a counter-argument, but it also does not actively exonerate anyone.
translations.t0015: The secondary employment concerns a scheduling app for dog groomers — a non-competing, insignificant startup belonging to a school friend. Favre disclosed it voluntarily and characterised it himself as 'the least industrial-espionage-adjacent thing in the world'. There is no evidenced connection between the secondary employment and Kestrel or MERIDIAN. The Winterthur card transactions date from September and October, not from the night of the offence.
translations.t0016: Favre describes the content of the secondary employment as clearly unrelated to espionage and shows emotional distress over the breach of contract.
translations.t0017: Card transactions in Winterthur predate the night of the offence by a wide margin and show routine purchases (MCC 5499 = food retail/kiosk).
translations.t0018: In her pre-interview assessment, the investigator notes sceptically 'Says he was away' — the location had not yet been verified prior to the interviews.
translations.t0019: Favre knew the real/decoy mapping (Confluence author, Iris's list of five), the current undocumented staging path (with the company since before 2023), the missing audit logging on scratch-02 (as builder), and the logging window (ticket author INFRA-2291). The perpetrator's knowledge would have been fully present. However, through his Confluence page at least 8 further accounts gained access to the real/decoy mapping, and approximately 40 people were aware of the logging window.
translations.t0020: Favre normally had physical access to the engineering floor. At the time of the offence, however, he was demonstrably in Val Müstair, approximately 4 hours from St. Gallen, without a car, dependent on the PostBus (last service at 16:10 according to his own Slack post on the day of the offence). The two 18-TB port arrays he had borrowed were in Colo Glattbrugg with intact seals and did not return until Monday — they could not have been the device used.
translations.t0021: The exfiltration began at 21:10 UTC (23:10 CEST) on Friday and ended at 03:58 UTC (05:58 CEST) on Saturday. Favre did not write messages independent of Andrin Caduff's Slack activity at 22:05 CEST on the preceding evening — but his out-of-office message had been active since 18:05 on Thursday. From Saturday 13:01 onwards he is demonstrably active in the incident channel via screenshare from Val Müstair. No card, badge, or other data points place him in St. Gallen or en route there at the time of the offence.
translations.t0022: The Confluence page remained accessible with eng-all permission until at least October 2025, despite Iris Ammann's ticket (SEC-402, April 2025) and Favre's own promise to address it. This is an organisational failure that genuinely widened the pool of potential perpetrators — without constituting direct incriminating evidence against Favre himself.
translations.t0023: The identities of the 9 accounts that read the Confluence page are not listed by name in the available case files. It cannot be ruled out that the perpetrator's account is among them and acquired the knowledge through this route — which directs the investigation towards the 8 other readers.
translations.t0024: Favre's physical absence in Val Müstair throughout the entire offence window is corroborated by multiple independent sources: an automatic out-of-office reply sent before the offence period (Thu 18:05), a public Slack announcement on Thursday afternoon, Slack messages from Val Müstair on the day of the offence (Sat 13:09 and 13:11), an independent witness statement from Lukas Hofer regarding the 4-hour video call, and a public expression of thanks in the incident channel. He explicitly stated that he has no car and is dependent on the PostBus. The two borrowed port arrays were demonstrably in Colo Glattbrugg with intact seals. Not a single data trail places him in St. Gallen at the time of the offence. The remaining incriminating points (dissemination of knowledge via Confluence, delayed ticket handling) are organisational failures without a bearing on perpetration. The deduction of 0.13 from the confidence score reflects that no train ticket, no card transaction for the journey there, and no independent Val Müstair source (e.g. a family member of the girlfriend) are present in the case files, and that interview statements remain assertions by nature.
translations.t0025: Although Yannick Favre possessed complete perpetrator knowledge and infrastructural access, he was demonstrably in Val Müstair throughout the entire offence window (Fri 23:10 – Sat 05:58 CEST), approximately four hours from St. Gallen, without a car and without any data point placing him at the scene. The incriminating points (Confluence page, ticket delays) are credibly explained as good-faith oversights and are supported by third-party statements.
translations.t0026: No train ticket or card record for the journey to Val Müstair on Thursday, 9 October is present in the case files.
translations.t0027: The 9 Confluence reader accounts are not listed by name in the case files; the actual perpetrator could be among them.
translations.t0028: No independent confirmation from Val Müstair (e.g. family members of the girlfriend, PostBus data) covering the entire period Thu–Sat.
translations.t0029: The garage log of Parkhaus Stickerei AG had not yet been evaluated at the time of the file handover (01.12.2025) — however, any entry matching Favre's number plate would in any case be irrelevant, since according to the case files he does not own a car.
translations.t0030: Favre's Jira comment in INFRA-2291 dated 11.10. at 07:30 ('Collector back up 06:00 as planned. Migration clean. (Automated message scheduled before I left.)') is declared as an automated message and therefore does not constitute evidence of his whereabouts at that time — it does, however, support the pre-planned departure date.
